name: Wonderful Jump
description: You are given an array of positive integers $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$$$ of length $$$n$$$. In one operation you can jump from index $$$i$$$ to index $$$j$$$ ($$$1 \le i \le j \le n$$$) by paying $$$\min(a_i, a_{i + 1}, \ldots, a_j) \cdot (j - i)^2$$$ eris. For all $$$k$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, find the minimum number of eris needed to get from index $$$1$$$ to index $$$k$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 4 \cdot 10^5$$$). The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le n$$$).
output_specification: Output $$$n$$$ integers — the $$$k$$$-th integer is the minimum number of eris needed to reach index $$$k$$$ if you start from index $$$1$$$.
approach_summary: Apply Knapsack and Basic Dynamic Programming paradigm under the Dynamic Programming (DP) framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
